title: Chapter III: Reunion Meetings
text:
Chapter III

Reunion Meetings

A narrative account of the first (August 6 and 7, 1938) reunion is given in Part I. At that meeting a plan of organization was adopted. Since then, reunions have been held, annually, always at Savoy, the seat of the old school. It is an announced policy of the Association to continue these reunions as long as interest will justify and there is a sufficient number to attend. Some have said that the reunions should be held as long as there remain as many as two of the old students physically and mentally able to attend. This will probably be done.

1939

The second reunion was held at Savoy, Sunday, August 6, 1939, with President Edgar Anderson McMahon presiding, and Mrs. Martha Buford May as secretary.

John Marcus Gist, of Sherman, conducted the opening services, in representation of a typical Monday morning chapel service of old Savoy College; a brief tribute to Harvey Johnson of Breckenridge, and an inspirational talk, of the type customarily given by President Halsell, was given by Bob Martin of Savoy.

Greetings on behalf of Choctaw Indian ex-students were extended by Bill Johnson of Durant, Oklahoma, and again tribute was paid to the memory of Professor Halsell and the old school.

Honorable J. R. May, Mayor of Savoy, delivered an impressive address of welcome on behalf of the citizenship, in which a tribute was again paid the old school and its founders.

Ninety-five members responded to roll call and to each was presented on the program booklet a thumbnail sketch of the history and activities of the old college.
